title: OpRecord
description: One line of ops.jsonl — the append-only operation log (timeline/op-log contract). Ops are immutable; rejection or history navigation appends a NEW operation instead of rewriting an old one. Current undo recomputes a journal prefix and records its result; the optional inverse field is retained only for historic snapshot-era replay. Mirrors cut_core::ops::OpRecord exactly.

op_id.description: Monotonic zero-padded id; ordering equals log order

via.description: Surface used: mcp | rest | cli | ui | internal

caller.description: Stable serialized identity of the original transport caller

verb.description: Fully-qualified verb name from schema/verbs.json, e.g. 'transcript.cut_words'

args.description: The verb args as received (shape per the verb's args schema)

rationale.description: Why the actor did it — shown verbatim in the review rail

effects.description: What actually changed on the timeline

inverse.description: Legacy snapshot-era undo payload. Current records omit it and recompute by replay; retained so historic journals and their old edit.restore records remain readable.

status.description: applied = normal; rejected = undone via review (the undoing itself is a new edit.restore op)
